Kupiskis Jewish Cemetery 2

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. This is the newer of Kupiškis's two Jewish cemeteries, established in the 19th century about 400 to 600 meters from its older counterpart and operating until 1941. Between July and September of that year, around 2,000 Jews from Kupiškis and the surrounding area were murdered here, in what became the town's principal Holocaust mass grave; a bilingual memorial now marks the site. Soviet authorities closed and destroyed the cemetery around 1970, using its gravestones to pave the town's streets — only a handful of Hebrew-inscribed tombstones survive at the edges of the former grounds today, restored after Lithuania regained independence in 1991. In a detail the source itself frames as an affront to the Soviet system that built it, a water tower now stands at the center of the former burial ground. Some local testimony suggests the cemetery was originally larger, encroached upon by a since-built apartment building and kindergarten, though this could not be confirmed from surviving maps.
